answer: Nectar-Ledger Operator Liability. Each new identity must be seeded by an existing operator, who posts a ferrous escrow covering the newcomer's first 90 days of activity limits. Any cluster flagged as one entity by shared timing and funding graphs causes the seeding operator's escrow to be slashed, not the sock-puppet wallets. Honest operators pay a small velvet insurance premium per seeded identity; a sybil farm of 1,000 identities costs its operator the full escrow per seed plus loss of seeding rights, making each fake identity a direct, repeated charge against the real party.
